title: Keep missing-series resolution counts compatible with int64 in both rule tables
answers: Why do missing-series resolution counts above 32,767 fail to save?
Support large missing-series evaluation counts on MySQL or PostgreSQL
How should missing-series resolution counts be stored in rule version history?
body:
Symptom: Saving a missing-series resolution count above 32,767 fails on MySQL or PostgreSQL.
Root cause: SMALLINT database columns could not represent the model’s int64 values; the correction lives in pkg/services/sqlstore/migrations/ualert/alert_rule_missing_series_evals_to_resolve.go:ExpandAlertRuleMissingSeriesEvalsToResolve.
Fix pattern: Widen both alert_rule and alert_rule_version columns together to nullable BIGINT; verify persistence in the current rule and its matching version, as in pkg/services/ngalert/store/alert_rule_test.go:TestIntegrationUpdateAlertRules using 43,200 evaluations.
Constraints: Preserve nullability and compatible ranges in both tables. This migration supplies backend-specific SQL for MySQL and PostgreSQL only; it provides no schema alteration for other backends.
applies: Changes to missing_series_evals_to_resolve persistence or its database range on MySQL and PostgreSQL.
